meta.title: The Man Who Built the Tram
meta.textType: functional: a talk about a person of the past, with a fact card

paragraphs: On Tuesday, April twenty-seventh, at two o'clock, the library held its History Hour. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat in a row of chairs with their notebooks. Guide Ann stood next to a big screen. The room was quiet, and everybody listened. She was a guide from the science museum. She smiled at the four friends. The screen showed an old drawing of a small tram with a conductor at the door. "Today I will tell you about a man of our old town," she said. "He was an engineer, and he built the first tram of our old town."

Next, Guide Ann showed a fact card on the screen. "The first line is his name," she said. "It says Engineer Paul, and it also says Pol." "Old papers have two spellings of his name," she added. "The second line shows his home, our old town." "Some cards have a line for nationality, but this card has none." "A nationality is the country that a person belongs to." "The old papers do not tell us." "The third line shows his job, engineer." "His first tram was opened in nineteen hundred and five, and he died in nineteen thirty-five." Mia wrote the two years in her notebook.

"Now look at the drawing again," said Guide Ann. "The first tram of the old town was built by him." "Children in school uniforms are climbing in, and so is a farmer with a basket." "The tram carried children to school and farmers to the market." "The man at the door is the conductor, and he holds up a ticket." "How long ago was that?" asked Mia. "It opened more than a century ago," said Guide Ann. "A century is one hundred years."

"Paul was born in a small village one hundred and fifty years ago." "He grew up there, and he loved numbers and machines." "He was a clever boy, and he liked to ask questions." "As a boy, he discovered an old clock in a shop." "He wanted to know how it worked." "Later, he studied engineering far away for four years." "Then he came home and built a tram for his town."

"The tram was a great success," said Guide Ann. "Many people used it every day, because a ticket cost very little." "Paul died in nineteen thirty-five, at the age of fifty-eight." "He is well known in our town today." "People still talk about him." "A small model of the tram is in the museum." Leo put up his hand and asked, "What is a conductor?" May looked at the drawing and said, "He is not the driver, and he holds a ticket." "So I think that he sells the tickets on the tram." "You are right," said Guide Ann with a smile.
